1 Dataset description

What the project is. The proposed project is a digital twin of a small road network: a 2 x 2 grid of signalised junctions (left-hand traffic, two lanes per direction, 200 m blocks) in which cars follow the Intelligent Driver Model and each junction’s traffic light is driven by a controller. The aim is to learn a signal controller from data (imitation of a max-pressure rule that is also aware of ambulances) and to evaluate it in closed loop.

Where the data comes from. No public dataset logs the internal state of a traffic signal together with the queues on every approach at every decision instant, so the dataset was generated with the project’s own simulator (traffic_twin, Python). Everything about the generating process (physics, signals, calibration of demand levels, random seeds, scenario mixture) is recorded in the data card DATACARD.md that ships with the data, and every column of every table is described in data_dictionary.csv. The simulator is deterministic: episode i uses seed 100000 + i, so any row can be regenerated.

1.1 Release front matter

The identity of a release is the pair (generator version, configuration hash) written to config.json; the head line of the data card repeats the row counts. Both are read here, not typed.

cfg  <- fromJSON(file.path(data_dir, "config.json"))
card <- readLines(file.path(data_dir, "DATACARD.md"))
head_line <- card[grep("generator_version", card)[1]]
grab <- function(pattern) as.integer(sub(paste0(".*?([0-9]+) ", pattern, ".*"), "\\1", head_line, perl = TRUE))
card_counts <- c(episodes = grab("episodes"), signal_ticks = grab("signal_ticks rows"), vehicles = grab("vehicles"))

front <- data.frame(
  item  = c("dataset", "generator_version", "config_hash", "episodes (data card)",
            "signal_ticks rows (data card)", "vehicles (data card)", "licence",
            "download link", "data card / dictionary"),
  value = c(basename(normalizePath(data_dir)), cfg$generator_version,
            sub(".*config_hash `([0-9a-f]+)`.*", "\\1", head_line),
            format(card_counts["episodes"], big.mark = ","),
            format(card_counts["signal_ticks"], big.mark = ","),
            format(card_counts["vehicles"], big.mark = ","),
            "CC BY 4.0 for the data, MIT for the generator code (proposed; synthetic data, no personal information)",
            "[DATASET_DOWNLOAD_LINK]",
            "DATACARD.md, data_dictionary.csv (shipped with the CSV files)"),
  row.names = NULL)
kable(front, caption = "Release front matter (read from config.json and DATACARD.md)")

The release contains five tables (CSV):

file one row per what it holds
episodes.csv episode the scenario settings (demand level, controller, sensor noise, ambulance rate, split) and the KPIs of the episode
vehicles.csv vehicle route, travel time, delay, stops, and the vehicle’s hidden driver parameters
signal_ticks.csv junction x decision instant the machine-learning table: what the controller could see, what it did, and two labels (y_mp_action, y_q_total_t30)
junction_1hz.csv junction x second queue and vehicle totals at 1 Hz, used to build the 30 s-ahead label
network_edges.csv directed road edge geometry and storage of each link

Each episode is 300 s warm-up + 3600 s main period + 300 s cool-down. Rows inside the warm-up, the cool-down and the last 30 s of the main period (the “tail”) are flagged and excluded from training.

1.2 File integrity (checksums)

If the release ships a SHA256SUMS.txt, every file is hashed again here and compared with it, so a reader can tell that the download is the file that was analysed.

# results="asis": cat() writes Markdown and the tables inside the if-blocks render as tables
sums_path <- file.path(data_dir, "SHA256SUMS.txt")
if (!file.exists(sums_path)) {
  cat("No `SHA256SUMS.txt` in `", data_dir, "`: checksum comparison skipped.\n\n", sep = "")
} else if (!requireNamespace("digest", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # fallback: list the md5 of each file (cannot be compared with a sha256 list)
  files <- read.table(sums_path, col.names = c("sha256_expected", "file"))$file
  cat(kable(data.frame(file = files, md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(data_dir, files)))),
            caption = "digest not installed: md5 of each file (not comparable with SHA256SUMS.txt)"), sep = "\n")
} else {
  sums <- read.table(sums_path, col.names = c("sha256_expected", "file"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  sums$size_MB <- round(file.size(file.path(data_dir, sums$file)) / 1e6, 1)
  sums$sha256_computed <- sapply(sums$file, function(f) digest::digest(file = file.path(data_dir, f), algo = "sha256"))
  sums$match <- sums$sha256_expected == sums$sha256_computed
  short <- function(h) paste0(substr(h, 1, 12), "...")
  cat(kable(data.frame(file = sums$file, size_MB = sums$size_MB, expected = short(sums$sha256_expected),
                       computed = short(sums$sha256_computed), match = sums$match),
            caption = "SHA-256 of each released file vs SHA256SUMS.txt (first 12 hex digits shown)"), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n**All checksums match:**", all(sums$match), "\n\n")
}

2 Loading and structure

2.1 Reading the tables

The CSV files were written by Python, so boolean columns contain the strings True / False. A small helper turns those into R logicals.

fix_bool <- function(df) {
  # convert character columns that only contain "True"/"False" to logical
  for (col in names(df)) {
    x <- df[[col]]
    if (is.character(x) && all(x %in% c("True", "False"))) df[[col]] <- (x == "True")
  }
  df
}

t0 <- Sys.time()
ep  <- fix_bool(read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "episodes.csv")))
vh  <- fix_bool(read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "vehicles.csv")))
st  <- fix_bool(read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "signal_ticks.csv")))
jz  <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "junction_1hz.csv"))
net <- fix_bool(read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "network_edges.csv")))
dd  <- fix_bool(read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "data_dictionary.csv")))
ep$ev_rate <- as.character(ep$ev_rate)       # "0" / "default", keep as text
cat("Loaded in", round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")), 1), "seconds\n")
## Loaded in 11 seconds

2.3 Cross-check against the data card and the data dictionary

The row counts are compared with the head line of the data card (a printed check, because a re-generated release changes them), and the data dictionary is compared with the files: if they agree, the number of dictionary rows per table equals the number of columns and every column name is documented. The stopifnot() calls only guard structural facts (unique keys, every column documented), which must hold for any release.

count_check <- data.frame(table = names(card_counts),
                          rows_in_file = c(nrow(ep), nrow(st), nrow(vh)),
                          rows_in_data_card = unname(card_counts))
count_check$match <- count_check$rows_in_file == count_check$rows_in_data_card
kable(count_check, caption = "Row counts: files vs the head line of DATACARD.md")
Row counts: files vs the head line of DATACARD.md
table rows_in_file rows_in_data_card match
episodes 120 120 TRUE
signal_ticks 300598 300598 TRUE
vehicles 360443 360443 TRUE 
dict_counts <- dd %>% count(table, name = "columns_in_dictionary")
file_counts <- data.frame(table = names(tables), columns_in_file = sapply(tables, ncol), row.names = NULL)
check <- full_join(file_counts, dict_counts, by = "table") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(undocumented = {
    cols <- names(tables[[table]])
    if (is.na(columns_in_dictionary)) NA_integer_ else sum(!cols %in% dd$column[dd$table == table])
  }) %>% ungroup()
kable(check, caption = "Columns per table: file vs data dictionary")

stopifnot(!any(duplicated(ep$episode_id)),
          !any(duplicated(st[, c("episode_id", "junction_id", "t")])),
          !any(duplicated(vh[, c("episode_id", "veh_id")])),

2.4 The features of the ML table

signal_ticks.csv is the table a controller model learns from. The data dictionary tags every column with a namespace and with twin_observable, which says whether the digital twin could present that column to a controller at run time. Keys, time stamps, the controller’s own actions and the labels are not observable; everything else is a legitimate feature.

ns <- dd %>% filter(table == "signal_ticks") %>%
  group_by(namespace, twin_observable) %>%
  summarise(columns = n(),
            examples = paste(head(column, 4), collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(twin_observable), desc(columns))
kable(ns, caption = "signal_ticks columns by namespace (full dictionary in the appendix)")
signal_ticks columns by namespace (full dictionary in the appendix)
namespace twin_observable columns examples
state TRUE 20 q_N, n_N, q_N_l0, q_N_l1
ev TRUE 16 ev_present_N, ev_dist_N, ev_eta_N, ev_q_ahead_N
downstream TRUE 12 down_n_N, down_occ_N, down_blocked_N, down_n_E
neighbour TRUE 12 nb_N_exists, nb_N_phase, nb_N_green_toward_me, nb_E_exists
sensor TRUE 4 obs_q_N, obs_q_E, obs_q_S, obs_q_W
signal TRUE 3 phase, time_in_phase_s, max_green_remaining_s
time FALSE 5 t, tick_idx, is_warmup, is_cooldown
action FALSE 4 action_requested, action_applied, forced, switched
key FALSE 2 episode_id, junction_id
label FALSE 2 y_mp_action, y_q_total_t30 
cat("Observable feature columns:", sum(ns$columns[ns$twin_observable]),
    " non-feature columns:", sum(ns$columns[!ns$twin_observable]), "\n")
## Observable feature columns: 67  non-feature columns: 13

In words: the signal namespace is the state of the light (which approach is green and for how long), state holds the queue and vehicle counts per approach and lane plus the arrivals of the last 30 s, downstream says how full and whether blocked each exit link is, neighbour is the phase of the adjacent junction, ev is the GPS-style ambulance channel and sensor is a noisy copy of the four queue lengths (obs_q_*). The full table with data types, units and null policy is in the appendix.

2.5 Missingness

na_table <- function(d, name) {
  n <- colSums(is.na(d))
  n <- n[n > 0]
  if (length(n) == 0) return(data.frame(table = name, column = "(none)", n_missing = 0, share = 0))
  data.frame(table = name, column = names(n), n_missing = as.integer(n), share = round(n / nrow(d), 4), row.names = NULL)
}
bind_rows(na_table(ep, "episodes"), na_table(vh, "vehicles"),
          na_table(st, "signal_ticks"), na_table(jz, "junction_1hz")) %>%
  kable(caption = "Columns with missing values (all others are complete)")

The missing values are all by design: the ambulance KPIs are NA in episodes without ambulances, gridlock_t is NA when no gridlock happened, enter_t is NA for vehicles that were still waiting in an entry queue when the episode ended (they never entered the network), exit_t is NA for those and for vehicles still on the network at the end, and the regression label y_q_total_t30 looks 30 s ahead, so it cannot exist on the last 30 s of the main period or in the cool-down. We verify the last claim directly:

st %>%
  mutate(period = case_when(is_warmup ~ "warm-up", is_cooldown ~ "cool-down",
                            is_tail ~ "tail (last 30 s)", TRUE ~ "main")) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(rows = n(), label_missing = sum(is.na(y_q_total_t30)),
            share_missing = round(mean(is.na(y_q_total_t30)), 4)) %>%
  kable(caption = "y_q_total_t30 missingness by period")

gridlock_eps <- ep$episode_id[ep$gridlock]
if (nrow(missing_main) == 0) {

} else {
  cat("Main-period rows without `y_q_total_t30`, by episode (episodes that ended early by the gridlock rule: ",
      if (length(gridlock_eps)) paste(gridlock_eps, collapse = ", ") else "none", "):\n\n", sep = "")

}

A main-period row can only lack the label when the episode ended early by the gridlock rule, so the last 30 s before the stop have no future to look at; that is the case for episode(s) 74, 93.

# the training population: main-period rows with none of the three flags set
main <- st %>% filter(!is_warmup, !is_cooldown, !is_tail) %>%
  left_join(ep %>% select(episode_id, demand_level, controller, split, sensor_noise_level, ev_rate),
            by = "episode_id")
cat("Main-period rows:", nrow(main), "of", nrow(st), "\n")

3.2 Delay distribution by demand level

Per-vehicle total delay = entry-queue wait + travel time - free-flow time, for cars spawned in the main period. Rule for the delay figures. Delay is right-skewed and spans two orders of magnitude, so every delay plot uses a log axis, and a log axis cannot show values at or below zero. The plots therefore keep only delays of at least 1 s; the vehicles dropped by that rule are counted below and are included in every table (which uses all cars). A delay below 1 s means the vehicle met no queue and no red light; a negative delay would mean that it drove faster than the free-flow reference (the reference uses the per-vehicle desired speed and a fixed turn penalty, so small negative values are possible in principle).

cars <- vh %>% filter(!is_warmup, vehicle_type == "car") %>%
  left_join(ep %>% select(episode_id, demand_level, controller, ev_rate, demand_asym), by = "episode_id") %>%
  mutate(demand_level = factor(demand_level, levels = lvl))
delay_min <- 1                                   # plotting threshold [s]
rule <- data.frame(
  cars_main_period = nrow(cars),
  delay_negative = sum(cars$total_delay_s < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  delay_below_1s = sum(cars$total_delay_s < delay_min, na.rm = TRUE),
  delay_missing = sum(is.na(cars$total_delay_s)),
  kept_for_plots = sum(cars$total_delay_s >= delay_min, na.rm = TRUE))
kable(rule, caption = "Cars affected by the plotting rule (delay >= 1 s); tables use all cars")
Cars affected by the plotting rule (delay >= 1 s); tables use all cars
cars_main_period delay_negative delay_below_1s delay_missing kept_for_plots
329727 36 61 0 329666 
share_dropped <- 1 - rule$kept_for_plots / rule$cars_main_period

The plotting rule drops 61 cars (0.02% of the main-period cars), of which 36 have a negative delay.

n_sample <- min(60000, rule$kept_for_plots)
cars_plot <- cars %>% filter(total_delay_s >= delay_min) %>% slice_sample(n = n_sample)   # cap for plotting
ggplot(cars_plot, aes(total_delay_s, fill = demand_level)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  facet_wrap(~ demand_level, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Per-vehicle total delay by demand level",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s-car sample, cars with delay >= %d s, log x-axis", format(n_sample, big.mark = ","), delay_min),
       x = "total delay [s]", y = "vehicles") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

The table separates finished trips (completed == TRUE, the vehicle left the network before the episode ended) from unfinished ones (still on the network or still in an entry queue at the end), whose delay is censored and would otherwise be mixed with the finished trips.

cars %>%
  mutate(trip = ifelse(completed, "finished", "unfinished")) %>%
  group_by(demand_level, trip) %>%
  summarise(vehicles = n(), mean_delay_s = round(mean(total_delay_s, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            median_delay_s = round(median(total_delay_s, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            p90_delay_s = round(quantile(total_delay_s, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable(caption = "Delay statistics by demand level, finished vs unfinished trips (all cars, main period)")
Delay statistics by demand level, finished vs unfinished trips (all cars, main period)

3.3 Mean delay by controller

One point per episode; the box shows the spread over episodes of the same controller. Because demand is the dominant factor, the plot is split by demand level; combinations without episodes are simply absent (free x-axis per panel), and the number of episodes behind each box is printed above it. The table gives the mean and a 95% t-interval over episodes (NA when a box holds a single episode).

ep_plot <- ep %>% mutate(demand_level = factor(demand_level, levels = lvl))
box_n <- ep_plot %>% group_by(demand_level, controller) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), y = max(mean_total_delay_s), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(ep_plot, aes(controller, mean_total_delay_s, fill = controller)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = box_n, aes(controller, y, label = paste0("n=", n)), vjust = -0.6, size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.18))) +
  facet_wrap(~ demand_level, scales = "free", ncol = 4, drop = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Mean car delay per episode, by controller and demand level",
       subtitle = "one point per episode; n = episodes in the box",
       x = NULL, y = "mean total delay [s/veh]") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

ep %>% group_by(demand_level, controller) %>%
  summarise(episodes = n(), mean_delay_s = mean(mean_total_delay_s),
            ci_half = ifelse(n() > 1, qt(0.975, n() - 1) * sd(mean_total_delay_s) / sqrt(n()), NA),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean_delay_s, ci_half), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  arrange(factor(demand_level, levels = lvl), controller) %>%
  kable(caption = "Mean delay by (demand level, controller) with a 95% t-interval half-width over episodes")

3.4 Fairness: delay by entry node

A signal controller can be efficient on average and still starve one arm of the grid. The entry node (origin in vehicles.csv: N0, N1, E0, … are the boundary nodes of the four sides) is a natural protected group for this check. The bar is the mean over episodes of the per-episode mean car delay from that origin; the whisker is the 95% t-interval over episodes.

fair_ep <- cars %>%
  group_by(episode_id, demand_level, demand_asym, origin) %>%
  summarise(mean_delay = mean(total_delay_s, na.rm = TRUE), cars = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(side = substr(origin, 1, 1))
fair <- fair_ep %>%
  group_by(demand_level, origin, side) %>%
  summarise(episodes = n(), mean_delay_s = mean(mean_delay),
            ci_half = ifelse(n() > 1, qt(0.975, n() - 1) * sd(mean_delay) / sqrt(n()), 0), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(fair, aes(origin, mean_delay_s, fill = side)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_delay_s - ci_half, ymax = mean_delay_s + ci_half), width = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ demand_level, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(title = "Mean car delay by entry node (origin)",
       subtitle = "mean over episodes of the per-episode mean; whiskers = 95% t-interval over episodes",
       x = "entry node", y = "mean total delay [s/veh]", fill = "side") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

fair_ratio <- fair %>% group_by(demand_level) %>%
  summarise(worst_origin = origin[which.max(mean_delay_s)], best_origin = origin[which.min(mean_delay_s)],
            worst_over_best = round(max(mean_delay_s) / min(mean_delay_s), 2), .groups = "drop")
kable(fair_ratio, caption = "Largest / smallest mean delay over origins, per demand level")

  summarise(episodes = n_distinct(episode_id), mean_delay_s = round(mean(mean_delay), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = side, values_from = mean_delay_s) %>%

Half of the episodes use the ns_heavy asymmetry (north and south entries spawn more cars), so a higher delay on the N/S arms is expected there; the ratio of the worst to the best origin is the number to watch when controllers are compared later.

3.5 Queue over time at the four junctions of one episode

One design-demand episode driven by max_pressure with ambulances is picked (the first such episode in the table). q_total is the number of queued vehicles (v < 2 m/s) on the four approaches of a junction, logged every second. The shaded bands are the warm-up and the cool-down.

pick <- ep %>% filter(demand_level == "design", controller == "max_pressure", ev_rate == "default") %>%
  arrange(episode_id)
ep_id <- if (nrow(pick) > 0) pick$episode_id[1] else ep$episode_id[1]
ep_info <- ep %>% filter(episode_id == ep_id)
jz %>% filter(episode_id == ep_id) %>%
  mutate(junction = paste0("J", junction_id)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(t, q_total)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = cfg$warmup_s, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.12, fill = "grey40") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = cfg$warmup_s + cfg$main_s, xmax = cfg$warmup_s + cfg$main_s + cfg$cooldown_s,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.12, fill = "grey40") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ junction, ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Episode %d (%s demand, %s): queued vehicles per junction at 1 Hz",
                       ep_id, ep_info$demand_level, ep_info$controller),
       x = "time [s]", y = "q_total [veh]")

3.6 Label balance of y_mp_action

The imitation label is the approach (0 N, 1 E, 2 S, 3 W) that the priority-aware max-pressure teacher would give green to. Because the label is recomputed from every row regardless of which controller drove the episode, the classes are roughly balanced; an excess of N and S reflects the ns_heavy demand asymmetry in half of the episodes.

lab <- main %>% mutate(y = factor(y_mp_action, levels = 0:3, labels = c("0 (N)", "1 (E)", "2 (S)", "3 (W)")))
balance <- lab %>% count(y) %>% mutate(share = round(n / sum(n), 3))
kable(balance, caption = "Label balance of y_mp_action on main-period rows")

3.7 Hidden driver aggressiveness alpha against delay

Every vehicle has a latent aggressiveness alpha ~ Beta(2, 2) that scales its desired speed, acceleration and headway. It is in vehicles.csv but not observable by a controller. Does it matter for the vehicle’s delay? The scatter uses a log y-axis, so it applies the same rule as above (finished trips with delay >= 1 s); the table and the correlation use all finished trips, including the ones the log axis cannot show.

alpha_all  <- cars %>% filter(completed)
alpha_pool <- alpha_all %>% filter(total_delay_s >= delay_min)
n_alpha <- min(60000, nrow(alpha_pool))
alpha_plot <- alpha_pool %>% slice_sample(n = n_alpha)
ggplot(alpha_plot, aes(alpha, total_delay_s)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.08, size = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "cs"), colour = "firebrick") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  facet_wrap(~ demand_level, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Hidden aggressiveness alpha vs total delay",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s finished trips with delay >= %d s (%d dropped by the log axis); red = GAM smooth",
                          format(n_alpha, big.mark = ","), delay_min, nrow(alpha_all) - nrow(alpha_pool)),
       x = "alpha (0 = timid, 1 = aggressive)", y = "total delay [s], log scale")

alpha_all %>%
  mutate(alpha_bin = cut(alpha, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2), include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(alpha_bin) %>%
  summarise(vehicles = n(), mean_delay_s = round(mean(total_delay_s), 1),
            mean_free_flow_s = round(mean(free_flow_time_s), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable(caption = "Mean delay by alpha bin (all finished trips)")

## Spearman correlation alpha vs delay (all finished trips): -0.013

The dependence is weak (Spearman rho = -0.013): in a queue everybody waits for the signal, so delay is dominated by the demand level and the controller rather than by the driver. This is reassuring for the project, because a controller cannot see alpha.

3.8 Ambulance versus car delay

In the episodes with ev_rate == "default" (84 of 120), ambulances (faster, more aggressive vehicles drawn from their own random stream) enter the grid at 4 per hour per entry node. In this version they are subject to the same signals as cars: the controllers that drove the episodes do not give them priority, so their delay is of the same order as a car’s, and only their shorter headway and higher desired speed make a difference. The teacher label y_mp_action encodes what a priority-aware rule would have requested; whether that reduces ambulance delay is a closed-loop question for the project, not something this table can show. The boxplot applies the same plotting rule as the other delay figures (delay >= 1 s on a log axis); the table uses all vehicles.

ev_eps <- ep$episode_id[ep$ev_rate == "default"]
vtype <- vh %>% filter(!is_warmup, episode_id %in% ev_eps) %>%
  left_join(ep %>% select(episode_id, demand_level), by = "episode_id") %>%
  mutate(demand_level = factor(demand_level, levels = lvl))
ev_dropped <- sum(vtype$total_delay_s < delay_min, na.rm = TRUE)
ggplot(vtype %>% filter(total_delay_s >= delay_min), aes(vehicle_type, total_delay_s, fill = vehicle_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  facet_wrap(~ demand_level, ncol = 4) +
  labs(title = "Total delay: ambulances vs cars (episodes with ambulances)",
       subtitle = sprintf("vehicles with delay >= %d s (%d dropped by the log axis)", delay_min, ev_dropped),
       x = NULL, y = "total delay [s], log scale") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

vtype %>% group_by(demand_level, vehicle_type) %>%
  summarise(vehicles = n(), mean_delay_s = round(mean(total_delay_s, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            median_delay_s = round(median(total_delay_s, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            mean_stops = round(mean(n_stops), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable(caption = "Ambulance vs car delay by demand level (all vehicles of the ambulance episodes)")

4 A simple feasibility model

Question. Can the teacher’s request y_mp_action be recovered from the feature row alone? If a shallow model manages it, learning a controller from this table is feasible.

Protocol. Features are the observable columns of the dictionary (twin_observable == TRUE) minus the noisy sensor copies obs_q_*: the signal state, the per-approach counts, the downstream and neighbour columns and the ambulance channel. Keys, period flags, the controller’s own actions and the labels are excluded. The split is by episode (split column), never by row, because consecutive rows five seconds apart are near-duplicates. The model is a depth-5 rpart tree, fitted on the train episodes and scored on the test episodes.

observable <- dd$column[dd$table == "signal_ticks" & dd$twin_observable]
sensor     <- dd$column[dd$table == "signal_ticks" & dd$namespace == "sensor"]
features   <- setdiff(intersect(observable, names(main)), sensor)
cat(length(features), "features:\n"); print(features)

Rather than describing the tree by hand, a helper reads the fitted object: which condition is at the root, which variables appear at each depth, and how the accuracy differs between rows with and without an ambulance in sight.

tree_story <- function(fit) {
  fr    <- fit$frame
  node  <- as.integer(rownames(fr))        # rpart node numbers: children of k are 2k and 2k+1
  depth <- floor(log2(node))
  lab   <- labels(fit)                     # the condition that leads INTO each node
  is_split <- fr$var != "<leaf>"
  vars_by_depth <- tapply(as.character(fr$var[is_split]), depth[is_split],
                          function(v) paste(unique(v), collapse = ", "))
  list(root = lab[node == 2],              # condition of the left child = the root split
       by_depth = data.frame(depth = as.integer(names(vars_by_depth)) + 1,
                             split_variables = unname(vars_by_depth)),
       n_leaves = sum(!is_split),
       vars_used = unique(as.character(fr$var[is_split])))
}
ev_in_sight <- function(d) d$ev_present_N | d$ev_present_E | d$ev_present_S | d$ev_present_W
acc_by_ev <- function(pred, d) {
  ev <- ev_in_sight(d)
  data.frame(rows = c("ambulance in sight", "no ambulance"),
             n = c(sum(ev), sum(!ev)),
             share_of_rows = round(c(mean(ev), mean(!ev)), 3),
             accuracy = round(c(mean(pred[ev] == d$y_mp_action[ev]), mean(pred[!ev] == d$y_mp_action[!ev])), 3))
}
story_raw <- tree_story(fit_raw)
cat("Root split:", story_raw$root, "\n")
## Root split: ev_present_W< 0.5
kable(story_raw$by_depth, caption = "Variables used at each depth of the raw-feature tree")

Reading (generated from the fitted tree). The root split is ev_present_W< 0.5; the variables used, from the top down, are ev_present_W, ev_present_E, ev_present_N, n_S, n_N, ev_eta_W, ev_dist_E (10 leaves). The ambulance channel appears among the split variables: when an ambulance is close to a stop line the teacher asks for that approach, which a single threshold can express. Rows without an ambulance in sight are 79.8% of the main-period rows; on those the label is the plain max-pressure rule, which compares differences of counts (n_a - mean(down_n) across approaches, with hysteresis against the current phase). A depth-5 tree over raw counts cannot express those comparisons, so its accuracy on the no-ambulance rows stays at 0.388.

4.1 The same tree with the pressures computed from the row

The max-pressure rule is a function of the row, so we can compute the pressures from the observable columns (this is exactly what the twin will do at run time) and offer them to the tree:

dirs <- c("N", "E", "S", "W")
add_pressure <- function(d) {
  # pressure_a = n_a - mean(down_n over a's unblocked exits), as in the controller
  for (a in dirs) {
    total <- 0; count <- 0
    for (o in setdiff(dirs, a)) {
      ok    <- !d[[paste0("down_blocked_", o)]]
      total <- total + ifelse(ok, d[[paste0("down_n_", o)]], 0)
      count <- count + ok
    }
    # as.numeric(): keep one storage type in every split, which rpart::predict insists on
    d[[paste0("pressure_", a)]] <- as.numeric(ifelse(count > 0, d[[paste0("n_", a)]] - total / pmax(count, 1), -1e9))
  }
  P <- as.matrix(d[paste0("pressure_", dirs)])
  d$pressure_cur  <- as.numeric(P[cbind(seq_len(nrow(d)), d$phase + 1)])   # pressure of the current green
  d$pressure_best <- as.numeric(apply(P, 1, max))
  d$best_dir      <- as.numeric(apply(P, 1, which.max) - 1)
  d$pressure_gain <- d$pressure_best - d$pressure_cur
  d
}
train_p <- add_pressure(train); test_p <- add_pressure(test); ood_p <- add_pressure(ood)
features_p <- c(features, grep("^pressure_|^best_dir$", names(train_p), value = TRUE))

set.seed(42)
fit_p <- rpart(as.formula(paste("factor(y_mp_action) ~", paste(features_p, collapse = " + "))),
               data = train_p, method = "class",
               control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 5, cp = 0.001, minbucket = 50))
pred_p <- predict(fit_p, test_p, type = "class")
acc_p  <- mean(pred_p == test_p$y_mp_action)
acc_p_ood <- mean(predict(fit_p, ood_p, type = "class") == ood_p$y_mp_action)
cat(sprintf("Test accuracy (with pressures, depth 5): %.3f;  on stress episodes (test_ood): %.3f\n", acc_p, acc_p_ood))

# a compact text summary of both trees: size, splits used, accuracy
tree_summary <- function(fit, name, acc) {
  frame <- fit$frame
  data.frame(model = name, terminal_nodes = sum(frame$var == "<leaf>"),
             splits_on = paste(unique(as.character(frame$var[frame$var != "<leaf>"])), collapse = ", "),
             test_accuracy = round(acc, 3))
}

Reading (generated from the fitted tree). With the pressures available, the five-level tree reaches 81.5% accuracy on unseen episodes (46.6% without them). Its root split is best_dir< 0.5 and the variables it uses are best_dir, pressure_gain, ev_present_W, ev_present_E, phase, i.e. the tree picks the computed pressure columns first. The ambulance columns are still used, for the rows where the teacher overrides the pressures. The accuracy on the stress episodes is 75.2%, lower than on the test episodes, so the rule only partly transfers to a demand level never seen in training.

                     acc_no_ambulance_rows = c(acc_by_ev(pred_raw, test)$accuracy[2], acc_by_ev(pred_p, test_p)$accuracy[2]))

Test accuracy of the two trees on rows with / without an ambulance in sight
tree acc_ambulance_rows acc_no_ambulance_rows
raw features 0.800 0.388
raw + pressures 0.507 0.886

On the rows without an ambulance the pressure tree scores 0.886 against 0.388 for the raw tree; on the rows with an ambulance in sight it scores 0.507 against 0.800, so with only five levels the pressure tree spends its splits on the (far more frequent) max-pressure rows and gives up part of the ambulance rows; a model with more capacity is needed to get both. The remaining errors are the hysteresis and max-green corner cases that a depth-5 tree cannot carve out; a deeper tree or a boosted model (the plan for the final project) is expected to close part of that gap.

5 Results of the Python ML pipeline (if available)

The project’s Python pipeline (traffic_twin/ml.py) trains logistic regression, gradient boosting and a decision tree for Task A (imitation of y_mp_action) and ridge / gradient boosting for Task B (predicting y_q_total_t30). If its results.json is next to this report, the headline test metrics are pulled in; the section is skipped otherwise.

ml_path <- params$ml_results
if (!file.exists(ml_path)) {
  cat("No `", ml_path, "` found: ML pipeline results not shown.\n\n", sep = "")
} else {
  ml <- fromJSON(ml_path, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  same_release <- isTRUE(ml$n_episodes == nrow(ep)) && isTRUE(ml$n_main_rows == nrow(main))
  cat(sprintf("`results.json`: %d episodes, %d main rows (this report: %d episodes, %d main rows) -> **%s**\n\n",
              ml$n_episodes, ml$n_main_rows, nrow(ep), nrow(main),
              if (same_release) "same release" else "DIFFERENT release: the numbers below were computed on other data"))
  task_a <- bind_rows(lapply(names(ml$task_a$models), function(m) {
    s <- ml$task_a$models[[m]]$splits
    data.frame(task = "A: y_mp_action", model = m,
               test_bal_acc = round(s$test$balanced_accuracy, 3), test_macro_f1 = round(s$test$macro_f1, 3),
               ood_bal_acc = round(s$test_ood$balanced_accuracy, 3), ood_macro_f1 = round(s$test_ood$macro_f1, 3))
  }))
  cat(kable(task_a, caption = "Task A (classification) headline metrics from results.json"), sep = "\n")
  task_b <- bind_rows(lapply(names(ml$task_b$models), function(m) {
    s <- ml$task_b$models[[m]]$splits
    data.frame(task = "B: y_q_total_t30", model = m,
               test_mae = round(s$test$mae, 2), test_r2 = round(s$test$r2, 3),
               ood_mae = round(s$test_ood$mae, 2), ood_r2 = round(s$test_ood$r2, 3))
  }))
  nb <- ml$task_b$naive_baseline
  task_b <- bind_rows(task_b, data.frame(task = "B: y_q_total_t30", model = "naive (q_total now)",
                                         test_mae = round(nb$test$mae, 2), test_r2 = round(nb$test$r2, 3),
                                         ood_mae = round(nb$test_ood$mae, 2), ood_r2 = round(nb$test_ood$r2, 3)))
  cat(kable(task_b, caption = "Task B (regression) headline metrics from results.json"), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}

7 Limitations and next steps

  • It is simulated data. The physics (IDM drivers without reaction time, no lane changes, no pedestrians, two-colour signals) is a simplification and the numbers are only as realistic as the calibration (saturation flow 1631.35 veh/h/lane, inside the textbook range). Next step: validate one scenario against SUMO or a published intersection study.
  • The label is a rule, not the optimum. y_mp_action is what max-pressure with ambulance priority would do; imitating it can at best tie the teacher, and the data card notes that this teacher switches often and is worse than fixed time at high demand. Next step: use the 30 s-ahead queue label y_q_total_t30 for a model that predicts the effect of an action, and compare controllers in closed loop on paired seeds with t-based intervals.
  • Ambulances are a channel, not yet a benefit. The episodes were driven by controllers that do not use the ambulance channel, so the data show how ambulances fare without priority; any claim about the gain of priority has to come from the closed-loop comparison planned for the project.
  • Shallow model, truth features. A depth-5 tree on raw counts is a feasibility check, not the final model, and the noisy sensor copies (obs_q_*) were not used. Next step: gradient boosting with GroupKFold by episode, trained on obs_q_*, with balanced accuracy, macro-F1 and the stress episodes as the out-of-distribution test.

obs_q_N int16 veh sensor TRUE never Binomial(q_a, 1-p_miss) + Poisson(p_miss/2), p_miss = sensor_noise_level; = q_a at 0

ev_present_N bool ev TRUE never an ambulance is on the approach edge from arm N within ev_horizon_m of the stop line (GPS channel, no noise)
ev_dist_N float32 m ev TRUE never distance of the nearest ambulance to the stop line; -1 if none
ev_eta_N float32 s ev TRUE never ev_dist / max(v_ambulance, 3 m/s); -1 if none
ev_q_ahead_N int16 veh ev TRUE never queued vehicles in the ambulance’s lane ahead of it; -1 if none (input of the priority_mp teacher)
ev_present_E bool ev TRUE never an ambulance is on the approach edge from arm E within ev_horizon_m of the stop line (GPS channel, no noise)

ev_present_S bool ev TRUE never an ambulance is on the approach edge from arm S within ev_horizon_m of the stop line (GPS channel, no noise)

ev_q_ahead_S int16 veh ev TRUE never queued vehicles in the ambulance’s lane ahead of it; -1 if none (input of the priority_mp teacher)
ev_present_W bool ev TRUE never an ambulance is on the approach edge from arm W within ev_horizon_m of the stop line (GPS channel, no noise)

ev_q_ahead_W int16 veh ev TRUE never queued vehicles in the ambulance’s lane ahead of it; -1 if none (input of the priority_mp teacher)
action_requested int8 action FALSE imitation never phase requested by the driving controller
action_applied int8 action FALSE imitation never phase in force after the plant’s filter (the pending phase when a switch was accepted)
forced int8 action FALSE imitation never 0 none, 1 min_green, 2 max_green, 3 all_red, 4 starvation guard (an occupied approach had no green for starvation_s)
switched bool action FALSE imitation never a switch (all-red) started at this instant
y_mp_action int8 label FALSE all never request of the priority-aware teacher priority_mp recomputed from this row (label for imitation): the ambulance’s approach when ev_eta_a <= allred_min + startup lost time + ev_q_ahead_a x saturation headway, otherwise the max-pressure request; identical to the max-pressure request on every row without an ambulance
y_q_total_t30 float32 veh label FALSE all NaN on tail/cooldown rows or when the episode ended early q_total of this junction at the first whole second >= t+30 (junction_1hz)
